abstract: Platelet orientation offers a processing variable for balancing thermal transport and compliance in boron-nitride-filled silicone films for flexible thermal interfaces. We compared vertically oriented and randomly dispersed platelets at 20 vol% using the same silicone formulation and cure, with orientation assessed by cross-sectional microscopy. At 25 °C, through-plane thermal conductivity was 1.8 ± 0.2 W m−1 K−1 for aligned films and 0.9 ± 0.1 W m−1 K−1 for randomly filled films. The corresponding tensile moduli were 2.4 ± 0.3 and 2.2 ± 0.2 MPa. Values are means ± sample standard deviations from five independently prepared films per group; no statistical hypothesis tests were performed. Aligned films retained 92% of their initial thermal conductivity after 500 bending cycles at a 5 mm radius. Thus, alignment doubled the mean measured conductivity while producing a comparatively small increase in mean modulus. This processing route improved through-plane transport within the tested formulation and conditions, although the mechanism was not isolated: interfacial thermal resistance was not measured, and device-level temperature reduction remains untested.
discussion: Prolonged heating altered the extractability and mechanical response of the disulfide-containing polyester network. Extending treatment at 110 °C from 15 to 60 min increased the sol fraction after THF extraction from 8% to 19% and decreased the storage modulus at 1 Hz and 25 °C from 6.0 to 3.8 MPa. These means represent three separately prepared specimens per condition; without error estimates or statistical tests, their variability cannot be assessed. The combined changes are consistent with network rearrangement and/or chain scission, but do not distinguish their contributions. SEC of the soluble fraction, using polystyrene calibration, revealed a broader low-molar-mass shoulder after 60 min. This observation supports a change in the soluble population, rather than directly characterizing the insoluble network. The DSC glass-transition temperature remained approximately 42 °C within measurement resolution, and FTIR resolved no shift in the ester carbonyl position. Neither observation excludes low levels of ester cleavage. An otherwise matched ester-only network and end-group analysis would help distinguish disulfide-associated changes from ester cleavage; these tests remain proposed work. Although reprocessing motivates this study, the present measurements do not establish performance over reprocessing cycles, recyclability, or long-term creep resistance.
results: The fabricated 10-bit SAR ADC in 65 nm CMOS was characterized at room temperature with a 1.0 V supply and a sampling rate of 20 MS/s. Five dies were measured; the results reported here are from one representative die and are not averages across the five dies. With a 1.1 MHz sinusoidal input, the measured signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) was 57.2 dB and the spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) was 69.5 dB. SNDR decreased to 54.8 dB at an input frequency of 9.7 MHz, indicating lower dynamic performance at the higher input frequency under the same sampling conditions. Peak differential nonlinearity (DNL) was +0.45/−0.38 LSB, and peak integral nonlinearity (INL) was +0.72/−0.66 LSB. The ADC core consumed 0.62 mW, including the comparator, DAC switching, and SAR logic but excluding the external reference driver and clock generator. Its active core area was 0.018 mm², excluding pads. Power was not swept across temperature. These power and area boundaries delimit the reported core metrics; an advantage over prior converters cannot be established without a harmonized comparison.
